Let's remind ourselves of the relationship between ${\theta }_{R}$ and $\theta .$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14225277/assets/708bfa7367283d4be71b5df2c426862041b0a5ca939550e74f20e0e642856045.png)

Using ${\theta }_{R}={63}^{∘},$ let's calculate all possible values of $\theta .$

- If $\theta $ lies in the first quadrant, then $\theta ={\theta }_{R}={63}^{∘}.$

- If $\theta $ lies in the second quadrant, then $\theta ={180}^{∘}-{\theta }_{R}={180}^{∘}-{63}^{∘}={117}^{∘}.$

- If $\theta $ lies in the third quadrant, then $\theta ={180}^{∘}+{\theta }_{R}={180}^{∘}+{63}^{∘}={243}^{∘}.$

- If $\theta $ lies in the fourth quadrant, then $\theta ={360}^{∘}-{\theta }_{R}={360}^{∘}-{63}^{∘}={297}^{∘}.$

Therefore, in ascending order, $\theta $ can be equal to ${63}^{∘},$ ${117}^{∘},$ ${243}^{∘},$ and ${297}^{∘}.$
